title: Scoped PRD: Reserved Pools Autoscale & Burst with Tenant Isolation Controls
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Deliver a production-ready Reserved Pool autoscaling and burst policy system for Redwood Dedicated customers, combined with tenant isolation controls and console/API surfaces. The feature should enable predictable baseline capacity, controlled burst behavior to absorb spikes, and policy-based isolation to prevent noisy neighbors while maintaining cost-efficiency.
problem_statement: Customers running Redwood Dedicated request predictable reserved capacity for steady workloads but need controlled, temporary burst for short spikes without manual capacity commits. Current Dedicated offering supports static pools and simple autoscaling toggles but lacks burst policies, explicit isolation limits per tenant, and the console/API controls required by platform and infra teams to safely enable burst on multi-tenant GPU pools.
goals: Ship an autoscaling controller that respects reserved baseline capacity while allowing controlled burst above baseline for short durations
Expose burst policy configuration via API and Console (max burst tokens/sec, burst window, cooldown, per-tenant caps)
Implement tenant isolation controls so a bursting tenant cannot exhaust shared resources or cause SLA violations for others
Provide observability and billing signals for baseline vs burst usage and automatic fallbacks when contention is detected
Enable feature-flagged rollout to a small set of Dedicated customers and internal dogfood clusters
out_of_scope: Full rework of scheduling kernel or new placement engine (this PRD extends existing pool scheduler)
On-prem hardware procurement or physical migration tooling
Complex chargeback models beyond baseline vs burst metering (detailed billing will be follow-up)
functional_requirements: FR-1: Define 'reserved pool' baseline capacity and a configurable 'burst budget' (% of unused cluster capacity or absolute GPU units)
FR-2: Autoscaler must scale up to baseline committed capacity automatically (existing behavior) and optionally allow ephemeral burst up to configured limits
FR-3: Burst policy parameters per pool: max_burst_units, burst_window_seconds, cooldown_seconds, tenant_burst_cap (absolute units or percentage), priority_routing (boolean)
FR-4: API endpoints: GET/PUT /pools/{id}/burst-policy, POST /pools/{id}/burst-override (for emergency ops with audit trail)
FR-5: Console UI: pool detail page with a new 'Burst & Isolation' tab to view and edit policies, visualize baseline vs burst consumption, and toggle per-tenant caps

FR-6: Isolation controls: per-tenant soft and hard caps on concurrent inference requests and KV cache size; when soft cap is exceeded, degrade to lower-priority queue; when hard cap is exceeded, reject excess requests with clear error code (429 with reason 'pool_hard_limit')

FR-7: Fallback behavior: when pool-level contention is detected, automatic fallback to configured alternative model variant or lower-cost pool (policy-defined), with telemetry and customer-visible error reason
FR-8: Telemetry emitted for baseline utilization, burst utilization, burst events (start/end), throttles, fallbacks, and per-tenant cap violations
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-1: Burst decision latency under 50ms so serving path is not impacted
NFR-2: Autoscaler must not introduce more than 1% tail latency regression in p99 for stable traffic
NFR-3: Feature must be rollbackable via feature flag within 15 minutes
NFR-4: All control-plane API changes must be backward compatible for two releases
NFR-5: Access controls: edits to burst/isolation policies require 'team:infra' or 'role:customer-admin' RBAC permission
api_changes: Add GET /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/burst-policy (returns JSON with fields: enabled, max_burst_units, burst_window_seconds, cooldown_seconds, tenant_caps)
Add PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id} to accept burst_policy block in request body
Add POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/burst-override for emergency ops (requires audit header and reason)
Extend existing allocation API to return 'provision_type': baseline|burst and 'burst_reason' optional string
console_changes: Pool detail: new 'Burst & Isolation' tab with editable controls and a time-series chart of baseline vs burst usage
New modal for editing per-tenant caps with warnings and inline validation
Alerting config: pre-built alert templates for 'burst utilization > 80% for 5m' and 'tenant cap violations'
Rollout UI: an enable/disable toggle per pool behind a global feature flag with 'Preview' and 'Apply' flows
rollout_plan: Stage 0: API contract review and security assessment (week 0-1)
Stage 1: Internal dogfood on one internal Dedicated cluster, enable feature-flagged burst for non-critical tenants (week 2-3)
Stage 2: Invite 2-3 pilot customers (small, medium) with support on-call and SLA exemptions (week 4-6)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to GA behind billing and legal sign-off (week 7-10)
Rollback: disable feature flag + drain active burst allocations; autoscaler returns to baseline-only behavior
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Admin can configure and persist a burst policy via API and Console and values are validated server-side
AC-2: When burst is enabled, short spikes increase visible 'burst_units' consumption without exceeding max_burst_units in 95% of test scenarios
AC-3: Tenant soft cap triggers lower-priority queue and logs an event; hard cap returns 429 with 'pool_hard_limit' and is observable in logs
AC-4: Fallback to alternate pool or model occurs within configured policy window when sustained contention is detected and is logged as a burst-fallback event
AC-5: Telemetry for baseline and burst utilization surfaces in Console charts and matches recorded internal metrics within 5% error over 1h aggregation
AC-6: Security review sign-off completed and RBAC enforces edit permissions for burst/isolation controls
AC-7: Performance: deploying autoscaler + burst does not regress p99 tail latency by more than 1% during a controlled load test
AC-8: Feature can be disabled via feature flag and the system returns to pre-launch behavior without residual resource reservations
monitoring_and_metrics: Alert: burst_utilization > 90% for 3m -> P1 ops page
Dashboard: per-pool baseline vs burst cost and tokens-per-second breakdown
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Noisy neighbor still destabilizes cluster despite caps -> Mitigation: implement hard caps enforced by scheduler with early rejection and fast telemetry
Risk: Billing surprises from unmanaged burst usage -> Mitigation: require explicit customer opt-in and surface expected cost impact in Console prior to enable
Risk: Autoscaler oscillation under bursty traffic -> Mitigation: introduce hysteresis via burst_window_seconds and cooldown_seconds, and test with synthetic traffic patterns
Risk: Security misconfiguration allows unauthorized edits -> Mitigation: RBAC gating, audit logs, mandatory security review
notes: Design already reviewed with Design team; small UI iteration expected after pilot feedback
Eng suggested initial soft-cap implementation using token-rate queuing to avoid scheduler complexity
Legal requested explicit opt-in language for burst billing in pilot contract templates
Follow-up PRD planned to define billing granularity and chargeback rules after pilot
